reviews.shortreason: The quote directly states that SNI-GNN predicts remote embeddings in-network to reduce the need for frequent synchronization.
The quote gives the stated 3.4×–20.5× acceleration, 59% memory-access reduction, less than 1% test-accuracy influence, and names both datasets.
The quote says more-connected nodes are selected for prediction and that sampling_ratio trades prediction accuracy against computational load.
The quote explicitly describes adaptively skipping broadcasts and quantization-aware communication to reduce broadcast-message size.
The quote only says the prediction method is shown in Algorithm 1; it does not state that the predictor is trained online during every run.
The quote lists Sift's components but does not state that its historical-embedding evaluator runs on a SmartNIC or another in-network accelerator.
The quote explicitly says ARIMA's computational cost makes it unsuitable for real-time in-network processing.
The quote explicitly says physical network communication for boundary nodes is skipped during a stale epoch, contrary to broadcasting them.
